correctness.rationale: The cut-edge identity yields \(\mathcal K=A/x+C/(x+(m-1)y)+\sum_j c_j/z_j\). Inverse-trace strict convexity and edge injection guarantee unrestricted uniqueness. KKT equations produce the mixed and deleted phases and check equality at t*. The beta-integral Riemann sum establishes the long-tail law. The packaged verify.py produced 7437 cross-checks including full independent edge-Laplacian construction and feasible perturbations; numerical evidence is supplementary.

originality.rationale: The full 2006 Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi barbell analysis, Yang 2014 unweighted clique/path extremality, and Bianchi et al. 2016 degree-weighted lollipop asymptotics address related but distinct claims. None of the inspected passages proves an exact heterogeneous-price lollipop conductance optimum and complete deletion threshold. The same formula could still have an unindexed equivalent elsewhere.
residual_risks: An unindexed prior derivation or a non-obvious corollary in broader resource-allocation literature may give the same exact formula.
Finite bibliographic searching does not prove historical uniqueness.

value.rationale: The lollipop is a canonical dense-core/path bottleneck graph in resistance and commute-time theory. The all-size price threshold, forced edge deletion, exact independent-edge optimum, and \(\ell^{-3/2}\) long-tail core share determine meaningful structural and asymptotic design behavior, not just numerical recomputation.
